elements.quote: This systematic review provides a comprehensive overview of ER behavioral observation and physiological measures of children and adolescents
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly identifies the report as a systematic review.

elements.quote: This systematic review provides a comprehensive overview of ER behavioral observation and physiological measures of children and adolescents, including their theoretical embedding and psychometric properties.
elements.reason: The abstract states the main objective of the review.

elements.quote: We included empirical studies assessing ER as an outcome variable in children and adolescents aged 0-15 years using at least one behavioral or physiological ER measure. Studies on secondary literature were excluded.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

elements.quote: we conducted a systematic literature search in PubMed, PsycINFO, Psyndex plus, and Web of Science
elements.reason: The abstract identifies the information sources used but fails to report when each source was last searched.
The abstract does not specify the methods used to assess risk of bias in the included studies.

elements.quote: Measurement types, theoretical grounding, and psychometric properties (reliability, validity, objectivity) were extracted and compared across age groups using descriptive statistics and chi-square tests.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the methods used to synthesize the results.

elements.quote: A total of 516 studies met inclusion criteria.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of included studies but does not report the total number of participants or summarize relevant study characteristics.

elements.quote: Only 5% reported validity evidence, 62% reliability, and 20% objectivity. Few studies referenced an ER definition or empirically tested an ER model. LAB-TAB and Delay of Gratification tasks were the most common behavioral observation measures, whereas RSA and EEG dominated physiological measures.
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for the main outcomes.
The abstract does not report meta-analysis summary estimates, and the review appears to be a descriptive systematic review of psychometric reporting rather than a meta-analysis of effect sizes.

elements.quote: Behavioral observation was more frequently used in younger children, whereas physiological measures were more common in older children ( p < .001; V = .37).
elements.reason: The abstract indicates the direction of effect when comparing groups.
The abstract does not summarize important limitations of the included evidence.

elements.quote: ER measurement in children and adolescents is characterized by limited psychometric reporting and insufficient theoretical integration. This review provides an overview of available methods and their psychometric properties, facilitating the selection of appropriate measures for future research.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the results and their implications.
The abstract does not specify the primary source of funding for the review.
The abstract does not provide the register name and registration number.

elements.quote: Valid and reliable ER measures are needed to develop models for mental health promotion and treatment. ... ER measurement in children and adolescents is characterized by limited psychometric reporting and insufficient theoretical integration.
elements.reason: The abstract describes the current state of knowledge (limited psychometric reporting and theoretical integration) and the need for valid/reliable measures.

elements.quote: This systematic review provides a comprehensive overview of ER behavioral observation and physiological measures of children and adolescents, including their theoretical embedding and psychometric properties. ...
